headline: CPI came in line and the AI complex exploded; PPI at 8:30 is the last inflation read before September
client_frame: July CPI landed **exactly on consensus** on all four lines — headline +0.1% MoM / +3.4% YoY, core +0.2% / +2.5% — and that non-event was the bullish outcome. September hike odds fell from a coin flip to **hold 59.4% / hike 40.6%** on the live CME tape, VIX collapsed 4.8% to **14.55**, and the AI complex went vertical: CoreWeave **+19.3%**, Super Micro **+19.0%**, Lumentum **+13.6%**, CAVA **+14.2%**. Two cautions against reading this as all-clear. First, July CPI was collected *before* the Hormuz oil spike — gasoline actually fell 2.9% on the month, so the energy shock now in Brent near $89 simply is not in this data yet. It shows up in August and September prints, which is precisely the window the Fed is deciding in. Second, the $42B 10-year auction hours later cleared at **4.683%, the highest since 2007**, with bid-to-cover slipping to 2.53x from 2.59x. Equities got the relief; the long end did not. Today's PPI at 8:30 matters more than usual because it feeds core PCE, and Hammack — the most hawkish voice on the committee — speaks fifteen minutes before it. **No index made a new high**: the S&P closed 0.12% under its August 7 record and the Nasdaq 100 remains 2.99% below its June peak.

geo_headlines: **CPI in line, and the internals matter:** shelter +0.1% (two-thirds of the monthly rise), OER +0.3%, energy −1.5%, gasoline −2.9%, used cars +0.4%, airfares +2.2%. Core goods +0.20% after two negative months.

**The oil shock is not in this data.** July prices were collected before the Gulf of Oman escalation. Gasoline fell on the month while Brent is now near $89 — the pass-through lands in the August and September prints.

**$42B 10-year auction tailed into weakness:** 4.683% high yield, highest since 2007; bid-to-cover 2.53x vs 2.59x prior; indirects ~76.7%. Reuters framed it as bonds stagnating on the highest auction yield in 19 years.

**EIA crude build was +17.4M barrels** to 424.4M — the largest weekly gain since January 2023, against an expected 1.4M *draw*. The +9.07M aggregator figure flagged as unverified in yesterday's brief was wrong; this is the official number.

**Oil is falling anyway this morning:** Brent −1.5% to ~$87.69, WTI −1.2% to ~$82.04 on demand-forecast cuts — even with the blockade unresolved and the IEA projecting a 4.3M bbl/day production hit this year.

**Hormuz rhetoric hardened:** Trump claims 'total control' of the Strait; Iran's Strait Authority says it 'remains closed and will not be reopened' absent US concessions. CENTCOM tally now 59 redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded. Kpler has transits ~90% below the pre-war norm.
**Watch August 17:** the June interim MOU's 60-day negotiating window reportedly expires, with an Iranian source telling Reuters there are no talks on extending it.
**Canada's 50% Section 338 tariffs hit 12:01am ET August 19** on ~$20B of goods. LeBlanc has met US officials three times in three weeks; no deal confirmed.
**Bitcoin ignored CPI entirely** — $63,411 Wednesday close, −0.20%, with ETH $1,877.59.
